citations.anchor: it('401s every operation that is not on the public list'
citations.why: Sweeps every operation in the generated OpenAPI document and asserts a 401 for each one not on the explicit public list, so a route that lost its guard fails here.

citations.anchor: it('protects a route that carries no metadata at all'
citations.why: Pins the other half — absent @Public() metadata means the guard still demands a session, so being public is only ever explicit.

citations.anchor: it('rejects a pending (not-yet-active) user'
citations.why: A pending account is refused at sign-in with no cookie set, alongside the sibling test for a disabled account.

citations.anchor: it('rejects a live session whose account was suspended'
citations.why: Pins the per-request half: an already-issued session stops authenticating the moment the account leaves active status.

citations.anchor: it('rejects an unknown email'
citations.why: Runs through the shared expect401 helper that asserts status 401, body message 'Invalid credentials' and no set-cookie — the identical assertion the wrong-password, pending, disabled and no-credential cases use.

citations.anchor: it('answers an unknown address in the same time as a wrong password'
citations.why: Pins the timing half by comparing the measured refusal latency of an unknown address against a wrong password.

citations.anchor: it('404s an unknown token, without hinting that it is unknown'
citations.why: Asserts the 404 body carries only the bare 'Not Found' message, the same body the expired and already-spent token cases produce.

citations.anchor: it('rejects only one of two concurrent accepts of the same link'
citations.why: Fires two simultaneous accepts of one invite token and asserts exactly one succeeds, the other 404s, and the resulting state is consistent.

citations.anchor: it('lets only one of two concurrent redemptions of the same link through'
citations.why: The same race on the reset path: one redemption wins, the other is refused.

citations.anchor: it('revokes every live session — the old password does not outlive itself'
citations.why: Asserts every sessions row for the account is revoked once the reset link is redeemed.

citations.anchor: it('issues no session of its own — holding a link is not signing in'
citations.why: Pins the second clause: redeeming a reset sets no session cookie.

citations.anchor: it('revokes only the presented session, not the user’s others'
citations.why: Asserts the user's other sessions still authenticate after one is signed out.

citations.anchor: it('is idempotent with a bogus session cookie'
citations.why: Pins the always-succeeds clause, alongside the no-cookie and repeat-logout siblings.

citations.anchor: it('signs out every device the old password had signed in'
citations.why: Asserts the account's live sessions are revoked by a password change.

citations.anchor: it('keeps the caller’s own session alive when one is named'
citations.why: Pins the exception: the named session survives the eviction.

citations.anchor: it('stores the session token’s digest, never the token'
citations.why: Reads the sessions row and asserts the stored key is the SHA-256 of the cookie value, not the value.

citations.anchor: it('stores a password as bcrypt at cost 12'
citations.why: Pins the bcrypt(12) clause against the stored credential.

citations.anchor: it('stores only the hash — the raw token is not in the database'
citations.why: Pins the link-token clause: the minted reset token is absent from the tokens table, only its digest is there.

citations.anchor: it('stores the SHA-256 of the secret, never the secret'
citations.why: Pins the API-token clause. The one clause left unpinned is the SSO-attempt token: nothing asserts the sso request row's id is the SHA-256 of the browser handle.

citations.anchor: it('mints a token and returns the plaintext exactly once'
citations.why: Asserts the mint response carries the secret and that a subsequent list carries neither secret nor tokenHash — the 'never a repeat response' clause.

citations.anchor: it('never writes the secret or its hash into the log'
citations.why: Pins the activity-log clause end to end.

citations.anchor: it('lets no event of any kind carry the secret or its hash'
citations.why: Pins the domain-event clause across created/revoked/used.

citations.anchor: it('accepts the exact 12-character floor'
citations.why: Pins the lower bound, with the sibling 'under the minimum length' test pinning the refusal below it.

citations.anchor: it('counts the ceiling in bytes, so a 72-character accented passphrase is rejected'
citations.why: A 144-byte, 72-character passphrase is refused with 400 rather than truncated to 72 bytes; the 'accepts the exact 72-byte ceiling' sibling pins the boundary from the other side.

citations.anchor: it('refuses a second row differing only in case'
citations.why: Inserts straight through Drizzle, bypassing the service layer, so the refusal can only come from the database-level case-insensitive unique constraint.

citations.anchor: 'refuses to delete the %s system role'
citations.why: Runs over all three system roles, asserting the delete rejects and the row is still there with isSystem true.

citations.anchor: it('is idempotent — a second run changes nothing'
citations.why: Pins the idempotency clause of seeding.

citations.anchor: it('survives two instances seeding at once'
citations.why: Pins the concurrent-boot clause.

citations.anchor: it('grants exactly the catalogue, by enumeration'
citations.why: Asserts the admin role's grant set equals the full permission catalogue key for key.

citations.anchor: it('contains no wildcard, in any role'
citations.why: Pins the second clause across every system role.

citations.anchor: it('delegates the all-of decision to AccessPolicy, with the caller’s grants'
citations.why: Substitutes a spying AccessPolicy and asserts the session guard asks it rather than deciding itself.

citations.anchor: it('delegates the decision to AccessPolicy instead of deciding itself'
citations.why: Pins the other delegate — the content API's bearer guard routes its decision through the same AccessPolicy.

citations.anchor: it('gates listing a member’s sessions on users:update, not the weaker users:read'
citations.why: Reads the route's permission metadata and asserts it is users:update; the sibling pins the revoke route.

citations.anchor: it('403s a viewer reading even their OWN session list'
citations.why: The same gate over HTTP: users:read is not enough, even for one's own list.

citations.anchor: it('marks the caller’s own session as current'
citations.why: Asserts current is true when an admin lists their own sessions.

citations.anchor: it('lists a member’s live sessions'
citations.why: Pins the 'only' half: listing another member's session asserts current is false.

citations.anchor: it('rejects an empty workspace bucket'
citations.why: An empty workspaceIds array is a 400 — the non-empty-set clause.

citations.anchor: it('rejects a bucket naming a workspace that does not exist'
citations.why: Pins the 400-rather-than-a-token-into-nowhere clause; the sibling covers a bucket mixing real and phantom ids.

citations.anchor: it('401s a bearer token minting another token — no self-issue'
citations.why: A demonstrably live bearer token is refused on the management routes; siblings cover list, revoke and a forged cookie header alongside the bearer.

citations.anchor: it('gates management on the tokens permissions'
citations.why: Pins the session half, though as a permission gate rather than a role gate — the dossier's wording 'an administrator's session' is looser than the code, which admits any role holding the tokens permissions.

citations.anchor: it('refuses a callback with no attempt cookie'
citations.why: Asserts the redirect Location equals the shared FAILURE constant (…/identity/signin?error=sso); the whole refusals block — foreign state, tampered response, unverified address, stranger, disabled, pending, provider decline — asserts that same one string.

citations.anchor: it('refuses when the provider itself declines'
citations.why: A failure originating in the adapter lands on the same identical redirect, so no reason is distinguishable from outside.

citations.anchor: it('burns the attempt before it exchanges anything, and outside the transaction'
citations.why: Asserts both clauses directly: the conditional consume happens before the adapter's complete() call, and the exchange runs with no transaction open.

citations.anchor: it('refuses a foreign state before it exchanges anything'
citations.why: Counts the fake provider's complete() calls and asserts it was never asked, so the state/attempt check really precedes the exchange.

citations.anchor: it('refuses to link an address the provider will not vouch for'
citations.why: A first sign-in with emailVerified false does not claim the existing account holding that address.

citations.anchor: it('refuses a disabled account, the same way the password path does'
citations.why: Pins the disabled clause over HTTP; the 'refuses a pending invite' sibling pins the pending clause.

citations.anchor: it('never demotes an account that already holds admin'
citations.why: The mapping handler naming a lesser role leaves an admin account on admin.

citations.anchor: it('ignores a role key this deployment does not have, and says so'
citations.why: An unknown role key leaves the role untouched and is logged rather than swallowed or fatal.

citations.anchor: it('refuses an empty domain allow-list even with no provider registered'
citations.why: JIT configured with an empty domain list fails plugin construction, so it can never be reached at runtime.

citations.anchor: it('refuses a domain that merely ends with an allowed one'
citations.why: Pins the exact-domain clause; evil-example.com is not admitted by an allow-list containing example.com.

citations.anchor: it('is idempotent, because providers retry'
citations.why: A replayed back-channel notice answers 200 with revoked 0.

citations.anchor: it('tells intermediaries not to cache the answer'
citations.why: Asserts the cache-control: no-store header on the response.

citations.anchor: it('404s for a provider nobody registered'
citations.why: Pins the 404 clause for a provider that cannot verify the logout token.

citations.anchor: it('refuses to build the app, naming the setting'
citations.why: Building the app with SSO providers registered and cookieSameSite strict throws, and the sibling asserts the message explains why.

citations.anchor: it('refuses to build with providers registered and cookieSameSite "strict"'
citations.why: The same refusal at the plugin-construction level, with the two allowed combinations pinned by its siblings.

citations.anchor: 'declares no %s, so no adapter inherits one from the port'
citations.why: Reads identity-domain's package.json and asserts both dependencies and peerDependencies are empty. The second clause — that identity-server's domain/ layer imports neither NestJS, Drizzle nor class-validator — has no test anywhere.

citations.anchor: it('reports a failed probe as unavailable, not unauthenticated'
citations.why: A rejected who-am-I query yields AuthStatus.Unavailable rather than the state that redirects to sign-in.

citations.anchor: test('says the server is unreachable instead of signing the user out'
citations.why: The browser-level half: a 500 from the probe renders the unavailable card rather than routing to the sign-in page.

citations.anchor: )('refuses every permission while %s', (status) => {
citations.why: A table over Loading, Unauthenticated and Unavailable asserting useHasPermission returns false in each; the no-provider-mounted sibling covers the fourth case.

citations.anchor: it('drops everything the outgoing session cached'
citations.why: Asserts every non-auth query is removed from the client on an identity change.

citations.anchor: it('keeps the current-user probe, which the caller re-seeds itself'
citations.why: Pins the exception: the auth namespace survives the sweep.
